logic_node.action: Avoid dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers for HF treatment
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, dihydropyridine calcium channel-blocking drugs (e.g., amlodipine, felodipine) are not recommended as treatment for HF. They may be used for hypertension if blood pressure remains elevated despite optimization of GDMT.

source_text: In patients with HFrEF, dihydropyridine calcium channel-blocking drugs are not recommended treatment for HF. (COR 3: No Benefit, LOE A)

logic_node.action: Avoid vitamins, nutritional supplements, and hormonal therapy for HF treatment
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, vitamins (D, E, thiamine), nutritional supplements (coenzyme Q10, carnitine, taurine), and hormonal therapies (testosterone, growth hormone, thyroid hormone) are not recommended other than to correct specific deficiencies. Vitamin E may cause potential harm.

source_text: In patients with HFrEF, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and hormonal therapy are not recommended other than to correct specific deficiencies. (COR 3: No Benefit, LOE B-R)

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, nondihydropyridine calcium channel-blocking drugs (diltiazem, verapamil) are not recommended. They are myocardial depressants and generally not well tolerated. Diltiazem was associated with higher risk of recurrent HF in HFrEF after acute MI.

source_text: In patients with HFrEF, nondihydropyridine calcium channel-blocking drugs are not recommended. (COR 3: Harm, LOE A)

logic_node.action: Avoid class IC antiarrhythmics and dronedarone
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, class IC antiarrhythmic medications (encainide, flecainide) and dronedarone may increase the risk of mortality. Sotalol (class III) also increased mortality in HF post-MI. Amiodarone and dofetilide are the only antiarrhythmics with neutral effects on mortality in HFrEF.

source_text: In patients with HFrEF, class IC antiarrhythmic medications and dronedarone may increase the risk of mortality. (COR 3: Harm, LOE A)

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, thiazolidinediones (rosiglitazone, pioglitazone) increase the risk of worsening HF symptoms and hospitalizations due to fluid retention via PPARgamma-mediated sodium reabsorption in the kidney.

source_text: In patients with HFrEF, thiazolidinediones increase the risk of worsening HF symptoms and hospitalizations. (COR 3: Harm, LOE A)

logic_node.action: Avoid saxagliptin and alogliptin in patients with HF
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk, the DPP-4 inhibitors saxagliptin and alogliptin increase the risk of HF hospitalization and should be avoided in patients with HF. The FDA recommends discontinuation of saxagliptin and alogliptin in patients who develop HF. Sitagliptin and linagliptin did not show this risk.

source_text: The DPP-4 inhibitors saxagliptin and alogliptin increase the risk of HF hospitalization and should be avoided in patients with HF. (COR 3: Harm, LOE B-R)

logic_node.action: Avoid NSAIDs or withdraw whenever possible
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, NSAIDs (both nonselective and COX-2 selective inhibitors) worsen HF symptoms and should be avoided or withdrawn whenever possible. NSAIDs cause sodium and water retention and blunt the effects of diuretics via prostaglandin inhibition.

source_text: In patients with HFrEF, NSAIDs worsen HF symptoms and should be avoided or withdrawn whenever possible. (COR 3: Harm, LOE B-NR)

logic_node.action: Avoid sotalol due to increased mortality risk
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF post-MI, sotalol (class III antiarrhythmic) was associated with increased mortality in the SWORD trial. Sotalol may be used for refractory atrial-ventricular arrhythmias with close monitoring for decompensation, but caution is warranted.

source_text: In the SWORD trial of the class III antiarrhythmic sotalol, patients with HF post-MI had increased mortality. Sotalol may be used for refractory arrhythmias with close monitoring.

logic_node.action: Amiodarone and dofetilide are neutral-effect antiarrhythmics in HFrEF
logic_node.action_detail: Amiodarone and dofetilide are the only antiarrhythmic agents with neutral effects on mortality in clinical trials of patients with HFrEF. They may be used when antiarrhythmic therapy is needed.

source_text: Amiodarone and dofetilide are the only antiarrhythmic agents with neutral effects on mortality in clinical trials of patients with HFrEF.

logic_node.action_detail: Doxazosin (alpha-1 blocker) exacerbates underlying myocardial dysfunction with moderate magnitude of HF precipitation. Should be used with caution in patients with HF.

source_text: Table 13: Doxazosin exacerbates underlying myocardial dysfunction, magnitude moderate, LOE B.

logic_node.action_detail: Nifedipine (dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker) exacerbates underlying myocardial dysfunction via negative inotropy with moderate magnitude of HF precipitation.

source_text: Table 13: Nifedipine exacerbates underlying myocardial dysfunction, magnitude moderate, LOE C, negative inotrope.

logic_node.action_detail: Disopyramide (class IA antiarrhythmic) exacerbates underlying myocardial dysfunction with major magnitude of HF precipitation.

source_text: Table 13: Disopyramide exacerbates underlying myocardial dysfunction, magnitude major, LOE B.
